text:
The Rangers arrive on a three-game winning streak, the latest a 4-3 win at SEA two days ago, but they're without defenseman Sean Durzi. Braden Schneider has moved in beside Pettersson and is up to 20:22 a night from 18:11. The Oilers, 3-1-1 in their last five after beating VAN 4-2, are missing Isaac Howard, and they already beat New York 4-1 on Nov. 1. Edmonton also hands the Rangers a sizable gap in goaltending: Joonas Korpisalo (NYR, projected) has made one start this season, and Devon Levi (EDM, projected) sits at -1.1 goals saved above expected, meaning he has let in about one more goal than the shots he faced would normally allow.

Our model expects a close one, 3.11 goals for EDM and 2.93 for NYR. At five on five the teams are nearly level in expected goals (NYR 52%, EDM 49%), meaning the share of chance quality each side creates. The Oilers' results run ahead of that: 4.11 goals a game, helped by a power play worth 0.86 expected goals a game and 4.56 penalties drawn a night.

Connor McDavid brings an 18-game point streak and our highest point probability on the night, 93%. Leon Draisaitl has the best goal chance at 49%, with goals in three straight. For the Rangers, Alexis Lafrenière (28% to score) was drafted first overall in 2020, and CBS Sports noted he slid two helpers in the win at SEA.
